content.text:
Saved the [research and examples](/Users/cysp/src/cyspbot/docs/research/wrangler-new-config.md).

Wrangler’s “new config” is an experimental TypeScript model:

- `cloudflare.config.ts` defines the Worker, bindings, and triggers.
- Optional `wrangler.config.ts` defines build and development settings.
- `--x-new-config` enables it; functions support configuration by mode.

Cloudflare describes it as available for testing and part of the foundation for the upcoming `cf` CLI. [Announcement](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-08-miniflare-v5/)

**For cyspbot, I recommend an isolated prototype before migration.** On the installed Wrangler 4.127.0, build, dry run, and local development worked. However, standalone `types --x-new-config` fails, and `--config` is rejected—both affect existing scripts. Development generates types automatically, but that does not replace the current checks.

The API also changes between releases: 4.129.1 renames binding targets from `workerName` to `worker`. The note covers this, Vitest integration, configuration composition, and deployment ownership.

No application configuration changed.

**Wrangler 4.130.0 materially changes the earlier findings.** I updated the [research note](/Users/cysp/src/cyspbot/docs/research/wrangler-new-config.md).

The main improvements are:

- Object-form `defineWorker()` results now support ordinary object spread.
- Worker and Durable Object bindings can reference another config directly, preserving type information.
- Referenced configs resolve using the same mode. [Source changes](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/570526276722ae57b250268a8af48fe0b1eaf774/packages/config/CHANGELOG.md)

I verified composition and mode-dependent Worker references with 4.130.0 builds and dry runs. Local development also worked and generated types.

**The remaining gaps persist:** `types --x-new-config` still fails, `--config` is still rejected, and referenced Workers are not automatically started or deployed.

This makes shared source/deployment configuration substantially more practical, although migrating cyspbot still requires resolving its type-generation and test integration. Repository dependencies remain unchanged.

content.text:
Because **the new generator hasn’t been connected to the `types` command**. In 4.130.0, they use separate paths:

- **`wrangler types`** doesn’t register `--x-new-config`, so argument parsing rejects it before generation. Without that flag, the command explicitly loads the old configuration through `readConfig()` and calls the old `generateEnvTypes()` implementation.
